questions.stem: Which scheduling algorithm can potentially lead to starvation?
questions.explanation: SJF can lead to starvation because longer processes may be indefinitely delayed if shorter processes keep arriving.

distractorRationale.a: FCFS does not prioritize processes, so starvation is unlikely.
distractorRationale.c: RR gives each process a fair share of CPU time, preventing starvation.
distractorRationale.d: While complex, Multilevel Feedback Queue can be designed to prevent starvation.

questions.stem: Explain how ageing can be used to prevent starvation in Priority Scheduling.
markingGuide: Define starvation in the context of Priority Scheduling.
Describe how ageing increases the priority of waiting processes.
questions.explanation: Starvation occurs when low-priority processes never get CPU time. Ageing gradually increases the priority of a process the longer it waits, ensuring that it eventually gets executed.

questions.stem: In Round Robin scheduling, what determines the time a process can hold the CPU?
questions.explanation: In Round Robin scheduling, the time quantum is the fixed time a process can hold the CPU before being preempted.

distractorRationale.a: Priority is not considered in Round Robin.
distractorRationale.c: Burst time does not directly affect CPU holding time in RR.
distractorRationale.d: Arrival time determines order, not duration.

questions.stem: Discuss the trade-offs between using Shortest Job First (SJF) and Round Robin (RR) scheduling algorithms.
markingGuide: Identify the main advantage of SJF in terms of average waiting time.
Discuss the potential for starvation in SJF.
Explain the fairness of RR and its impact on turnaround time.
Compare the contexts where each algorithm might be preferred.
questions.explanation: SJF minimizes average waiting time but can cause starvation if short jobs keep arriving. RR is fairer, giving each process CPU time, but can increase turnaround time. SJF is preferred for batch systems, while RR suits interactive systems.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of Multilevel Feedback Queue scheduling?

options.text: All processes have the same priority.
It uses a single queue for all processes.

questions.explanation: In Multilevel Feedback Queue scheduling, processes can move between queues based on their behavior and requirements, allowing dynamic priority adjustment.

distractorRationale.a: Priorities can change as processes move between queues.
distractorRationale.c: Processes can have different priorities in different queues.
distractorRationale.d: It uses multiple queues, not a single queue.

questions.stem: What is the primary goal of CPU scheduling?
questions.explanation: The primary goal of CPU scheduling is to optimize overall system performance, which includes maximizing CPU utilization, minimizing waiting time, and maximizing throughput.

distractorRationale.a: While important, maximizing CPU utilization is not the sole goal.
distractorRationale.b: Minimizing waiting time is crucial, but not the only objective.
distractorRationale.c: Maximizing throughput is a goal, but there are other considerations.
